summary: jmrwd-gjdob-util ships an obfuscated in-manifest code loader that executes XOR-decoded bytes on require
details: On require of this package, index.js reads a numeric byte array from a non-standard `_b` field inside package.json, XORs each byte with 0x96, and stashes the resulting string on globalThis. lib/runner.js then compiles and runs that string via `Function('require','__dirname', <decoded>)(require, __dirname)`. The decoded payload in this version is a `console.log(1)` stub, but the mechanism is a generic staged loader: the manifest carries the actual JavaScript source as encoded data, hidden from normal inspection, and any republished version can swap in arbitrary code without touching the shipped JS. The package has an empty exports object, an empty README, and a random-looking name, so it provides no library functionality — the only effect of loading it is to execute attacker-controlled code reconstructed from a concealed manifest field. This is the characteristic shape of a staged npm dropper shell.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
